2026-08-17T12:30:52.4954403Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4954835Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4955183Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4955666Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4956141Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4956647Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4958929Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4960890Z >
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4963178Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4965550Z >
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4966320Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4967066Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4967239Z ### How to Use
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4967472Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4968444Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4969207Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4969385Z ```bash
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4970044Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4970767Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4971358Z ```
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4971553Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4971813Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4972328Z ```bash
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4972849Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4973622Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4974456Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4975531Z ```
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4975740Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4976491Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4977341Z ```bash
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4977906Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4978845Z ```
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4979054Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4979390Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4980155Z ```bash
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4980676Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4981535Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4982217Z ```
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4982418Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4982672Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4983090Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4984483Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4986076Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4987564Z ```bash
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4988086Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4989187Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4989994Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4990314Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4990821Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4991806Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4992588Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4993046Z ```
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4993246Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4993976Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4994865Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4995028Z ```bash
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4995689Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4996568Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4997274Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4997694Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4998097Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4999080Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4999612Z ```
2026-08-17T12:30:52.4999806Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.5000014Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-17T12:30:52.5000824Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-17T12:30:52.5001786Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-17T12:30:52.5002772Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-17T12:30:52.5003767Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-17T12:30:52.5004882Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-17T12:30:52.5005411Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.5005578Z ### Notes
2026-08-17T12:30:52.5005795Z 
2026-08-17T12:30:52.5006404Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-17T12:30:52.5007784Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-17T12:30:52.5009276Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-17T12:30:52.5010507Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-17T12:30:52.5011687Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-17T12:30:52.5012780Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-17T12:30:52.5013738Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-17T12:30:52.5015297Z </mcp-clis>
